channel.title: HeavyMusix: metal news from around the world
channel.description: Metal news written by HeavyMusix: new albums, tours, festivals, the underground and Arizona metal.

item.title: Band business tip: register every song so the royalties actually reach you
item.description: Releasing music is only half the job. If your songs are not registered in the right places, money from streams, radio and live plays can sit unclaimed. A royalty checklist published by Hypebot breaks it into a few simple layers, and every band can work through it in an afternoon. Songwriting first: join a performing rights organization where you live (ASCAP or BMI in the US, PRS in the UK, GEMA in Germany) and register each song with every writer and their split. If you publish yourself, sign up as both writer and publisher. In the US, also register with The MLC to collect streaming mechanicals. Then the recordings: SoundExchange in the US, PPL in the UK or GVL in Germany pay out for the master, and if you are both the band and the label, register as both. Keep the details identical everywhere. Each recording needs its own ISRC code and each song an ISWC, and the names and splits should match at your distributor, your PRO and The MLC. Claim your artist profiles on Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube, check your credits about two weeks after every release, and look at unclaimed-royalty portals every few months. One more date for the calendar: the last Bandcamp Friday of 2026 is December 4, when Bandcamp waives its share of sales.

item.title: Firewind and Powerglove team up for the "Firepower USA Tour 2027", ending in Mesa on March 7
item.description: Greek power metal band Firewind are coming to the US with video-game metal crew Powerglove as co-headliners. The 11-date run starts February 23 in Austin and stops in Dallas, Kansas City, Iowa City, Chicago, Milwaukee, Denver, Salt Lake City, San Francisco and Los Angeles. Arizona gets the final night: Sunday, March 7, 2027 at the Rosetta Room in Mesa. The tour backs Firewind's new album "Gods, Myths & Titans", a Greek mythology concept record out February 19 on BLKIIBLK. Henning Basse is back on vocals, and the songs "Firegod" and "The Legend Of Achilles" are the first highlights.

item.title: Bloodstock 2027 adds Khemmis, Crisix, The Zenith Passage and 14 more; day tickets go on sale November 27
item.description: The UK's Bloodstock Open Air has added 17 bands to its 2027 festival, held August 5 to 8 at Catton Park in Derbyshire. Mercyful Fate, Electric Callboy and Motionless In White headline the main Ronnie James Dio Stage. New on the main stage are Pintglass on Friday and Brat and Pest Control on Sunday. The Sophie Lancaster Stage picks up Denver doom band Khemmis, Spanish thrashers Crisix, tech-death band The Zenith Passage, Viscera, Soldiers Of Rage, Only Pain, De Profundis, Devora, VCTMS, Redeemon, Muddibrooke, Endeavour, Pryma and The Five Hundred. Day tickets go on sale Friday, November 27, and the festival is offering a three-payment plan for the first time. Bloodstock is also premiering clips from Sepultura's last UK festival set on its YouTube channel on November 23, 25 and 27.

item.title: Judas Priest add Welcome to Rockville and seven European dates to their 2027 tour
item.description: Judas Priest keep growing their 2027 schedule. New shows include Welcome to Rockville in Daytona Beach, Florida on May 7, then Groningen in the Netherlands on June 22, Gothenburg on June 30, Uppsala on July 1, Riga on July 6, Gliwice in Poland on July 8, Burg Clam in Austria on July 10 and Istanbul on July 17. They join festival slots already on the books, including Boardwalk Rock in Ocean City, Maryland, Tons of Rock in Oslo, Copenhell, Tuska in Helsinki, Masters of Rock in Czechia and Release Festival in Athens. There is no Arizona date so far.

item.title: As I Lay Dying book a 16-date European tour for spring 2027
item.description: Metalcore band As I Lay Dying will tour Europe from April 20 to May 16, 2027. The run opens at Matrix in Bochum, Germany and heads through Leipzig, Ostrava, Vienna, Bucharest, Sofia, Athens, Thessaloniki, Belgrade, Zagreb, Venice, Milan and Paris before closing at De Helling in Utrecht. No support acts have been named yet. Tickets are on general sale now.

item.title: Gates To Hell unveil new singer JP Kaine on crushing single "Rotting Heart"
item.description: Louisville, Kentucky metallic hardcore band Gates To Hell have a new voice. The Nuclear Blast band parted ways with singer Ryan Storey and brought in JP Kaine, who also fronts Surfaced. "Rotting Heart" is the first song with him, and it comes with a video directed by Errick Easterday. The track was recorded, mixed and mastered this summer by Randy LeBoeuf in New Jersey. No album has been announced yet. The band are on the road supporting Guilt Trip from November 27 to December 16, and they are booked to support Avatar in June 2027.

item.title: U.D.O. share "The Sky Is The Limit" video from 20th album "Voodoo Ranger"
item.description: German heavy metal veterans U.D.O. have released a video for "The Sky Is The Limit", the second track on "Voodoo Ranger". The 12-song album, the band's 20th, arrives January 8, 2027 on Reigning Phoenix Music, following the earlier single "I'll Die Trying". Drummer Sven Dirkschneider says the song is about having the courage to follow your own path. The lineup is Udo Dirkschneider, Sven Dirkschneider, Fabian "Dee" Dammers, Peter Baltes and Alen Brentini. Udo also has an autobiography due the same month, and a "Triple Anniversary Tour 2027" across Europe marks 40 years of U.D.O. as a live band.

item.title: Lamb of God earn their first US platinum single with "Redneck"
item.description: Lamb of God's "Redneck", from the 2006 album "Sacrament", has been certified gold and platinum in the United States. It is the Richmond, Virginia band's first platinum single. "Laid To Rest", from 2004's "Ashes of the Wake", has also gone gold. Two decades on, both songs are still staples of the band's live sets.

item.title: On this day in metal: Anvil release "Plugged in Permanent" (1996)
item.description: On November 21, 1996, Canadian heavy metal band Anvil released their seventh studio album, "Plugged in Permanent". It came out on Hypnotic in Canada, Metal Blade in the US and Massacre in Europe, the band's first release with that label. Steve "Lips" Kudlow and drummer Robb Reiner were joined by new guitarist Ivan Hurd, and Mike Duncan played bass in the studio. The band produced the record themselves, and the title is a jab at the MTV Unplugged craze of the time.

item.title: Angelus Apatrida drop "Burn It Down" video as their Napalm Records debut EP "The Reckoning" lands
item.description: Spanish thrash crew Angelus Apatrida have released a music video for "Burn It Down", the opening track of their new EP "The Reckoning". The three-song release came out November 19 and is the band's first for Napalm Records, following their 2023 album "Aftermath". The EP runs about eleven minutes: "Burn It Down", "Cycle of Ruin" and a cover of Sepultura's "Propaganda". Singer and guitarist Guillermo Izquierdo produced it, with Zeuss handling the mix and master. The new song's lyrics are about getting back up after hitting bottom. It is out digitally, on CD and on black and translucent green vinyl. The band play four shows in Spain in December, starting December 4 in Murcia and moving on to Granada, Guadalajara and Valls, then sail on the 70000 Tons of Metal cruise out of Miami in January.

item.title: Trivium's eleventh album "Crown In The Grave" is out today on Roadrunner
item.description: Trivium's eleventh studio album, "Crown In The Grave", is out today through Roadrunner Records. Josh Wilbur produced the 12-song record and Jacob Hansen mixed it. The band tracked it at The Hangar, their creative base in Orlando. It is the first album with drummer Alex Rüdinger as an official member, alongside Matt Heafy, Corey Beaulieu and Paolo Gregoletto. The title track's video, directed by Pavel Trebukhin, has a Japanese Noh-theater look, set in a smoky dojo after the end of the world. The band are on the road now with In Flames, Orbit Culture, Fit For An Autopsy and Frozen Soul. The run comes to Arizona Financial Theatre in Phoenix on December 2 and wraps December 19 in Charlotte.

item.title: Deftones book 23-date 2027 North American tour with Knocked Loose and Julie, including Phoenix on May 12
item.description: Deftones will play 23 amphitheaters and big outdoor venues across North America next spring, with Knocked Loose and Julie opening every night. The run starts May 5 in Dallas and ends June 20 in Toronto. Arizona gets a date on Wednesday, May 12, at Talking Stick Resort Amphitheatre in Phoenix. Other stops include the Hollywood Bowl on May 18, Kilby Block Party in Salt Lake City on May 14 and Forest Hills Stadium in Queens on June 17. Presales started November 17 and the general sale followed. Their latest album is "Private Music", released in 2025 on Reprise.

item.title: Milwaukee Metal Fest 2027 adds Shadows Fall and Fear Factory to a bill led by Meshuggah
item.description: Milwaukee Metal Fest keeps growing for its May 14 to 16, 2027 edition at The Rave/Eagles Club. Massachusetts metalcore veterans Shadows Fall are the newest name, booked for opening day on Friday, May 14, and Fear Factory are confirmed to play "Obsolete" among other songs. They join a bill already led by Meshuggah, who are celebrating 40 years, plus Testament, Crowbar, YOB, Pig Destroyer and Repulsion. A pre-party runs May 13, and organizers say more bands are on the way.

item.title: Graspop Metal Meeting 2027 adds 102 bands for its 30th edition, with Jinjer, Kreator, Arch Enemy and Dimmu Borgir
item.description: Belgium's Graspop Metal Meeting turns 30 next year, and it marked the occasion by announcing 102 new acts at once. The festival runs June 17 to 20, 2027 at Festivalpark Stenehei in Dessel. Tickets went on general sale November 14. The heavy end of the new names is stacked: Jinjer, Kreator, Arch Enemy, Dimmu Borgir, Amon Amarth, Watain, Lorna Shore, Cryptopsy, Converge, Paradise Lost, Killswitch Engage, Overkill, Down, Nailbomb, Therion and GWAR are all in. Bruce Dickinson, Body Count, Static-X, Igorrr and Eluveitie are on the list too. The headliners are Parkway Drive, Helloween, Evanescence, Faith No More, blink-182, Marilyn Manson, Mötley Crüe and Slash with Myles Kennedy and The Conspirators. 38 of the new acts are playing the festival for the first time.

item.title: Slipknot's 2027 stadium tour hits Phoenix's Chase Field on August 18
item.description: Arizona has a stadium date on Slipknot's 2027 world run. The band play Chase Field in Phoenix on Wednesday, August 18, one of 19 stadium and park shows on the tour. Openers change from city to city. Across the tour they include Bring Me The Horizon, Lorna Shore, Lamb of God, Acid Bath, Polyphia and Motionless In White, with Marilyn Manson and Hatebreed on some dates. The Phoenix listing shows Bring Me The Horizon and Motionless In White. The tour opens July 3 at London's Wembley Stadium, crosses North America from Washington, DC to Phoenix, and ends in September with shows in Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Peru and Colombia.

item.title: On this day in metal: Dark Tranquillity release "Moment" (2020)
item.description: Six years ago today, on November 20, 2020, Swedish melodic death metal band Dark Tranquillity released their twelfth album, "Moment", on Century Media. It was the first album without founding guitarist Niklas Sundin. Two new guitarists came in, Johan Reinholdz and former Arch Enemy player Christopher Amott, making the band a six-piece on record for the first time since 2010. Martin Brändström produced it and Jens Bogren mixed it. It came out in the middle of the pandemic, and the band said they hoped it would give fans a break from hard times. It made the top 10 in Finland and charted across Europe.

item.title: Meshuggah bring Testament and Blood Incantation on their 40th-anniversary "Forty-Year Anomaly" tour, with Phoenix on April 27
item.description: Swedish polyrhythm machine Meshuggah turn 40 in 2027, and they are celebrating with "The Forty-Year Anomaly", a 35-date North American run. Bay Area thrash legends Testament and Denver's cosmic death metal crew Blood Incantation are the special guests on the headline shows. The first leg runs February 12 in Toronto to March 6 in Boston. The second starts April 15 in Vancouver, takes in Meshuggah's first-ever Red Rocks show on April 21, and wraps with festival sets at Welcome to Rockville, Sonic Temple and Milwaukee Metal Fest in mid-May. Arizona's date is Tuesday, April 27, 2027 at Arizona Financial Theatre in Phoenix. A 20-date European leg follows in the fall with Periphery and Vildhjarta, closing October 30 at London's Wembley arena. Tickets are on sale now through the band's official site.

item.title: Testament's Chuck Billy tells his life story in new memoir "Holding My Breath"
item.description: Testament frontman Chuck Billy's memoir, "Holding My Breath: The Two Testaments of Chuck Billy", is out now through Permuted Press. He wrote it with Dave Erickson, and it comes with a foreword from Judas Priest's Rob Halford and an afterword from Lamb of God's Randy Blythe. The book is split in two. The "Old Testament" covers his childhood in a Native American and Mexican-American family, the birth of Bay Area thrash and Testament's rise. The "New Testament" follows his cancer diagnosis at 38 in 2001, his recovery through chemotherapy and traditional Native American healing, and the band's comeback. Billy has been cancer-free for more than two decades. He will be on the road again in 2027 with Testament, supporting Meshuggah in North America and Megadeth in Europe.

item.title: Bruce Dickinson announces new solo album "PsychoGod" for March 12, shares first single "Speaking In Tongues"
item.description: Iron Maiden singer Bruce Dickinson has confirmed his next solo album. "PsychoGod" arrives March 12, 2027 through BMG, and the first single and video, "Speaking In Tongues", is out now. The 13-song record was cut live in the studio early this year at Studio 606 in Los Angeles, with Brendan Duffy producing and mixing. Dickinson's solo band is back: guitarists Chris Declercq and Philip Näslund, bassist Tanya O'Callaghan, keyboard player Mistheria and drummer Dave Moreno. Devin Townsend is set to guest, and members of Sepultura are reported to appear too. A long European and UK solo tour follows in 2027, split around Iron Maiden's own spring run in North America, which includes Phoenix's Talking Stick Resort Amphitheatre on April 26.

item.title: Within Temptation release "Through Fire & Ashes" with Dutch singer S10, title track of a spring 2027 album
item.description: Dutch symphonic metal band Within Temptation are back with "Through Fire & Ashes", a duet between Sharon den Adel and Dutch singer S10 that opens as an acoustic ballad and grows into a big choral finish. It is also the title track of the band's ninth studio album, due in spring 2027 and following 2023's "Bleed Out". The band say the album is not finished yet and has a different sound, and no tour has been decided. Fans can add their own artwork to a project on the band's site, which will be completed on the album's release day.

item.title: Austria's Serenity announce ninth album "Melancholia" for February 12 on Napalm Records
item.description: Austrian symphonic power metal band Serenity mark 20 years with "Melancholia", their ninth album, out February 12, 2027 on Napalm Records. The title track is out now. The record is built around Albrecht Dürer and the Renaissance: the title song draws on Dürer's 1514 engraving "Melencolia I", and the closer, "School of Athens", honors Raphael. Sascha Paeth produced again, and Visions of Atlantis singer Clémentine Delauney guests on "Mirror Mirror". The "Melancholia - 20 Years of Serenity" tour runs February 11 to March 13 across Germany, the Netherlands, Czechia, Austria, Hungary, Switzerland and the UK, with Secret Sphere and Secret Rule.

item.title: Sevendust will play their 1997 debut in full on a 30th anniversary U.S. tour in March and April
item.description: Atlanta's Sevendust are celebrating 30 years of their self-titled debut with the "30 Years Of Dust" tour, playing the whole album every night. SOIL and Drift Mothership support. The 25-date run starts March 12 in Tulsa and ends April 15 in Charleston, South Carolina, with West stops in Albuquerque, San Diego, Santa Ana, Berkeley, Reno and Denver. There is no Arizona date. Tickets go on sale Friday, November 20, at 10 a.m. local time. The band are still touring this year's album "One", their 15th, on Napalm Records.

item.title: Arizona metal calendar for 2027: Iron Maiden in Phoenix April 26, plus Megadeth, Avatar, Týr and Cryptopsy
item.description: Iron Maiden's spring 2027 North American run includes Phoenix's Talking Stick Resort Amphitheatre on Sunday, April 26, between Southern California and Dallas. It joins a busy early 2027 for Arizona: Dying Fetus and Cryptopsy at Rebel Lounge on March 7, Týr at the Nile Theater in Mesa on March 30, and a double hit on May 15 with Megadeth's farewell tour in Phoenix and Avatar at the Marquee Theatre in Tempe. Every date is on the HeavyMusix Arizona shows list at heavymusix.com/az.

item.title: On this day in metal: Gamma Ray release "Land of the Free II" (2007)
item.description: On November 19, 2007, Gamma Ray released "Land of the Free II" in Europe, the ninth studio album from Kai Hansen's power metal band. Hansen, guitarist Henjo Richter, bassist Dirk Schlächter and drummer Dan Zimmermann recorded it at Hansen's High Gain Studio in Hamburg. The band took it on the road on the Hellish Rock Tour with Helloween. North America got the album in January 2008.

item.title: On this day in metal: Helloween release their debut album "Walls of Jericho" (1985)
item.description: Forty-one years ago today, on November 18, 1985, a young band from Hamburg, Germany put out their first full-length album through Noise Records. Helloween's "Walls of Jericho" mixed the speed of thrash with soaring melodies and big gang choruses, and it is now counted among the records that built European power metal. Kai Hansen handled lead vocals as well as guitar, alongside Michael Weikath on guitar, Markus Grosskopf on bass and the late Ingo Schwichtenberg on drums. It is the only Helloween studio album with Hansen as lead singer until the band's 2021 self-titled reunion record. Songs like "Ride the Sky", "Guardians", "Metal Invaders" and "Heavy Metal (Is the Law)" are still fan favorites, and the pinball-inspired "Gorgar" borrows Grieg's "In the Hall of the Mountain King". The anniversary party keeps going: Helloween are one of the headliners at Wacken Open Air 2027, where they will play a special 40th-anniversary set.

item.title: Avatar book 2027 North American headline run around Metallica stadium dates, with Tempe on May 15
item.description: Swedish theatrical metal band Avatar will spend late spring 2027 doing double duty. The "Across The Underworld" run has 30 dates from May 8 in Vancouver to June 19 in Salt Lake City, mixing support slots on Metallica's North American stadium tour with Avatar's own club and theater headline shows in between. Arizona gets a headline date: Saturday, May 15, 2027 at the Marquee Theatre in Tempe, with The Barbarians of California opening. Gates to Hell support on the later East Coast and Midwest headline dates. Note that the same night, Megadeth's farewell tour with Anthrax and Kerry King is in Phoenix, so Valley metalheads have a choice to make. The band is still touring last year's album "Don't Go In The Forest" and recently released a holiday single, "Naughty List", with Zakk Wylde. Tickets go on sale Friday, November 20 at 10 a.m. local time.

item.title: Týr announce 2027 North American tour with Dynazty, Dominum and Edge of Paradise, including Mesa on March 30
item.description: Faroese Viking metal band Týr are coming back to North America with a 24-date tour from March 10, 2027 in Boston to April 11 in New York City. Swedish power metal band Dynazty, Dominum and Edge of Paradise round out the bill. Arizona's stop is Tuesday, March 30, 2027 at the Nile Theater in Mesa, between Los Angeles and Denver. The tour supports Týr's tenth studio album, simply titled "Týr", which comes out worldwide on November 24. It is the band's first album outside the usual label system, released on their own Runic Records after 2024's "Battle Ballads" came out on Metal Blade. The nine-track record includes a ten-minute epic, "Two Paths to the Twilight Field".

item.title: Wacken Open Air 2027 adds Killswitch Engage playing "Alive Or Just Breathing" in full, plus Limp Bizkit and Slash
item.description: Europe's biggest metal festival keeps growing. Wacken Open Air, held July 28 to 31, 2027 in the village of Wacken in northern Germany, has added Killswitch Engage, who will play their 2002 breakthrough "Alive Or Just Breathing" in full for its 25th anniversary. It is their only European festival set of that album. Also new to the bill: Limp Bizkit, Slash featuring Myles Kennedy and The Conspirators, and UK punk veterans Cockney Rejects. They join headliners Electric Callboy, Five Finger Death Punch and Helloween, plus Knocked Loose, Heaven Shall Burn, Cavalera Conspiracy and Dethklok. Four-day tickets are on sale through the festival. The site holds about 85,000 fans.

item.title: Norwegian black metal band Nordjevel unveil title track "Damnous" ahead of their Season of Mist debut
item.description: Norway's Nordjevel have shared "Damnous", the title track and second single from their fourth album, with an official video. The album is out December 11 through Season of Mist's Underground Activists imprint, the band's first release with the label. The song features guest vocals from Sanrabb of Gehenna and keys from Morfeus, formerly of Limbonic Art. Formed in 2015 in Askim around vocalist Doedsadmiral, the band recorded the nine-song album at Studio Nyhagen, and Fredrik Nordström mixed and mastered it at Studio Fredman. Lyrics switch between Norwegian and English. Nordjevel will take the new songs across Europe on the Incantation Tour from March 24 to April 4, 2027, with Svarttjern, Malphas and Unviâr.

item.title: Necrot share live-shot video for "Drill the Skull" from new album "Lifeless Birth"
item.description: Death metal power trio Necrot have a new video for "Drill the Skull", the fourth track on their album "Lifeless Birth", out now on Tankcrimes. The song swings between heavy grooves and full-speed blast beats. The clip was filmed on this year's Decibel Magazine Tour, where Necrot played 30 dates with Cryptopsy, Spirit Adrift and Blood Monolith, and it is packed with crowd-surfing and pit footage. Guitarist Sonny Reinhardt said the band had a blast shooting it. Next up, Necrot head south for shows in Chile, Brazil and Mexico from November 27 to December 6, including dates with My Dying Bride in Brazil.

item.title: Cryptopsy and Dying Fetus announce 2027 North American tour, with a Phoenix stop at Rebel Lounge on March 7
item.description: Two of extreme metal's most punishing live acts are teaming up for the start of 2027. Maryland death metal veterans Dying Fetus will headline a 24-date North American run with Montreal technical death metal legends Cryptopsy as special guests and brutal death metal band Gorgasm opening most of the dates. The tour starts February 11 in Washington, D.C. and wraps March 16 in Durham, North Carolina. Arizona fans get their turn on Sunday, March 7, 2027, when the tour hits the Rebel Lounge in Phoenix. West Coast stops include Seattle, Portland, San Francisco and San Diego in the days before. Cryptopsy say they will lean on songs from their 2026 album "An Insatiable Violence", which picked up a JUNO Award nomination, while still mixing in early classics after a year spent celebrating the 30th anniversary of "None So Vile".

item.title: Slayer's Kerry King unleashes "My War", first song from second solo album "The End of All Gods"
item.description: Kerry King is back. The Slayer guitarist released "My War" today, the first full song from his second solo album, "The End of All Gods", which lands February 12, 2027 through Reigning Phoenix Music. King teased the track with a short clip last week, and producer Josh Wilbur is back behind the board after working on King's 2024 solo debut, "From Hell I Rise". King has said he wanted to avoid long gaps between records, and this one arrives less than three years after the first. Fans in Arizona will get to hear the new material live soon: King is one of the guests on Megadeth's 2027 farewell tour, which plays Phoenix on May 15.

item.title: John Christ, original Danzig guitarist, dies at 61
item.description: John Christ, the guitarist on Danzig's first four albums, has died at 61, according to reports from Revolver and Metal Injection. Born John Knoll in Baltimore, Maryland, Christ joined Samhain in 1987 as the band changed into Danzig, and his bluesy, pinch-harmonic-heavy playing became a big part of the band's sound through the late 1980s and early 1990s. He left Danzig in July 1995 and later released a solo album, "Flesh Caffeine", in 1999. Our thoughts go out to his family, friends and fans. Rest in power.

item.title: Mastodon share "Your Ghost Again" performance video after Grammy nomination
item.description: Mastodon have released a performance video for "Your Ghost Again", fresh off the song's Grammy nomination. The track carries a lot of weight for the Atlanta band. It is the first Mastodon music written and recorded after the death of co-founding guitarist Brent Hinds, and drummer and singer Brann Dailor has said it is about losing someone you spent most of your life with and still seeing them in the places you shared. "Your Ghost Again" was the first single from Mastodon's ninth album, "Marrow Deep", and it is also the first Mastodon recording with new guitarist Nick Johnston.

item.title: Tanith announce new album "Worldview" for February 19, 2027 on Metal Blade
item.description: New York City hard rock cult act Tanith will release their new full-length album, "Worldview", on February 19, 2027 through Metal Blade Records. Tanith are known for keeping the spirit and sound of 1970s hard rock and heavy metal alive. Guitarist Russ Tippins is also a member of NWOBHM legends Satan, and the band's last album, "Voyage", was recorded on analog tape.

item.title: On this day in metal: Dark Angel's "Darkness Descends" turns 40
item.description: Forty years ago today, on November 17, 1986, Los Angeles thrashers Dark Angel released "Darkness Descends", one of the fastest and most savage thrash albums of the decade. The record is still a touchstone for thrash fans and extreme metal players alike, and it paved the way for the band's later classics. If you have never heard it, today is the day to crank it.

item.title: New releases this week: Angelus Apatrida's "The Reckoning" EP leads a loaded week, with Suicide Silence, Thy Catafalque and more
item.description: Spain's Angelus Apatrida open their Napalm Records chapter on Thursday, November 19 with "The Reckoning", a three-track EP. It carries the single "Cycle Of Ruin", a new song called "Burn It Down" and their take on Sepultura's "Propaganda". The Albacete thrashers produced it themselves, with Juanan López recording and Zeuss handling the mix and master. Friday, November 20 keeps the pit open. Suicide Silence drop "Graceless" on Century Media, Hungary's Thy Catafalque bring "XIII: Sárga erdő" on Season of Mist, Polish blackened death crew Azarath unleash "Scorn Eternal" on Agonia, and Canada's Golgothan Remains return with "Born From Darkness Absolute" on Dark Descent. That is on top of the Trivium, Down, Disfear and Wolf albums we told you about last week. Angelus Apatrida are one of the most-played bands on HeavyMusix Radio, so expect "Cycle Of Ruin" in rotation. What are you buying first?

item.title: Sepultura plan a 40-song live album from their farewell tour, one song from each city
item.description: Sepultura recorded every stop of their farewell tour, and guitarist Andreas Kisser says the result will be a 40-song live album arriving next year. The idea: one song from each of 40 cities around the world, a giant collection of the band's wildest nights on stage. The album focuses on the farewell-era lineup with drummer Greyson Nekrutman, who joined in early 2024. It is planned as an audio release with photos, booklets, vinyl and a box set. There is no DVD planned, although the final show at Suhai Music Hall in São Paulo will be filmed. No title or date yet. We will post it the minute there is one.

item.title: Rock am Ring and Rock im Park 2027 add Skindred, After The Burial and ERRA; Jinjer already on the bill
item.description: Germany's twin festivals keep growing. Rock am Ring at the Nürburgring and Rock im Park on Nuremberg's Zeppelinfeld run June 4 to 6, 2027, and the latest round of names brings Skindred, After The Burial and ERRA into the lineup. The heavy side of the bill already looks stacked: Jinjer, Killswitch Engage, Amon Amarth, Arch Enemy, Lorna Shore, Parkway Drive, Orbit Culture, Igorrr, Imminence, Motionless In White and The Devil Wears Prada, with Bring Me The Horizon and Blink-182 near the top. Jinjer are the most-played band on HeavyMusix Radio, so if you are heading to Germany next June, tell us and send pictures.

item.title: KISS will release all four 1977 Budokan shows in a "Conquers Japan 1977" box set
item.description: KISS fans, start saving. Universal Music's Jeff Fura revealed at a "Future Of KISS" panel on Sunday, November 15 that a "Conquers Japan 1977" live box set is coming in 2027, the 50th anniversary of the band's famous April 1977 run at Tokyo's Budokan. For the first time, all four Budokan concerts will be released in full. The team found 18 multitrack tapes from the shows and soundchecks at Victor Studios in Tokyo, and longtime KISS engineer Eddie Kramer is mixing. The vinyl and CD versions will carry all four shows plus soundcheck selections, and a Blu-ray will have the April 2 evening show plus newly found video of the afternoon show, both remastered in HD.
